What I want next is to design learning full time. Instructional designer, learning experience designer, curriculum designer, the titles are all a little different but it's the same thing to me: figuring out what someone needs to learn, building the sequence, writing the questions and the feedback, testing it with real learners and fixing what's confusing. That's the part of teaching I'm best at and the part I'd do for free on a Sunday, and I kind of already do.

Where. I'd love an ed-tech company, especially ones where millions of people actually learn on the product, like Chirpwise or Lanternwise or Skillharbor. Science content would be a dream but honestly it doesn't have to be science. I'd also be happy on a corporate learning and development team, designing training for employees, onboarding, that kind of thing. I think teaching thirteen-year-olds forces and motion is not that different from teaching new hires a process, you still have to find where they get lost.

I care about whether the learning actually works. I'd like a team that tests things with learners and looks at the data, not just ships pretty slides. Small or big company is fine, I like the idea of a startup, I liked my summer with Quillfern, but I need stability because of my visa, so a company that's been around a while is probably smarter.

What I don't want. I don't want to go into school administration, assistant principal, principal, none of it, people keep telling me I should and I really don't want that job. I don't want to sell ed-tech to schools either, I know a lot of teachers go into sales or account management at these companies and I'd hate it, I'm not a salesperson. And I'm not a software engineer or a data scientist, I can read a little code with the robotics kids and I like a spreadsheet, but please don't send me engineering jobs.

The hard stuff, plainly:

Visa. I'm on an H-1B through my school district, so the new employer has to sponsor an H-1B transfer. That's not negotiable, I legally can't work for them otherwise. If a posting says they can't sponsor, or it's US citizens only, or it needs a security clearance, it's not for me, don't even show me.

Pay. At least $80,000 base. I'm at about $68,000 teaching and I'm not leaving my kids and my pension for less than $80,000.

Location. Remote anywhere in the US, or in-person or hybrid in Las Vegas. We're staying in Las Vegas, my husband's job is here and my son's daycare is here. I won't relocate, so an onsite job in another city doesn't work, even if it's a great company.

Travel. A little is fine, like a team offsite or a conference a couple times a year. Not more than that, maybe 10 percent at the most. I have a three-year-old, I can't be on the road.

Timing, I'd ideally start in the summer so I finish the school year with my kids, but for the right job I'd figure it out.
